rows.answer: Nike’s total revenues were **$46.3 billion in fiscal 2025** (year ended May 31, 2025), versus **$51.4 billion in fiscal 2024**—a **10% decrease on a reported basis** (9% currency-neutral). [1][2]

Nike’s gross margin declined 190 basis points to 42.7% in fiscal 2025 (year ended May 31, 2025), primarily because of higher discounts and channel-mix changes that reduced NIKE Brand average selling prices (ASP), as well as higher inventory-obsolescence reserves. [1][2]

Specific negative drivers were:
- Lower NIKE Brand ASP: approximately **180 basis points** of margin pressure, primarily from higher discounts and channel-mix changes. [1]
- Higher other costs: approximately **90 basis points**, including higher inventory-obsolescence reserves. [1]
- Lower Converse gross margin: approximately **20 basis points**. [1]
- Unfavorable net foreign-exchange-rate changes, including hedges: approximately **10 basis points**. [1]

These were partly offset by lower NIKE Brand product costs (+approximately 80 basis points), lower warehousing and logistics costs (+approximately 20 basis points), and prior-year restructuring charges (+approximately 10 basis points). [1]

Nike spent **$4,689 million** on demand creation in **fiscal 2025 (year ended May 31, 2025)**, up **9%** from **$4,285 million** in fiscal 2024. [1][2]

The increase was driven by higher **brand marketing expense**—including investment in key sports events—and higher **sports marketing expense**. Foreign-currency changes did not materially affect demand creation expense. [1]

NIKE Direct revenues declined 13% to **$18.8 billion in fiscal 2025** (year ended May 31, 2025), from **$21.5 billion in fiscal 2024**. They represented approximately **42% of total NIKE Brand revenues** in fiscal 2025. [1][2]

On a currency-neutral basis, NIKE Direct revenue declined 12%, driven by a 20% decline in NIKE Brand Digital sales; NIKE store sales were flat. [3]
Nike’s net income decreased **44%** from fiscal 2024 to fiscal 2025 (fiscal years ended May 31, 2024 and May 31, 2025, respectively), falling from **$5,700 million** to **$3,219 million**. [1]

Lululemon’s net revenue grew **10%** in fiscal 2024 (fiscal year ended February 2, 2025), increasing by **$968,848 thousand** to **$10,588,126 thousand**, from **$9,619,278 thousand** in fiscal 2023. [1]

In Lululemon’s FY2024 (fiscal year ended February 2, 2025), China Mainland comparable sales increased **25%** (**27% on a constant-dollar basis**), while Americas comparable sales **decreased 1%**. Comparable sales exclude revenue from the 53rd week of 2024. [1][2]

The provided excerpts do not state Lululemon’s consolidated operating margin for FY2024 (fiscal year ended February 2, 2025) or its year-over-year change.

They do report segment operating margins: Rest of World segmented income from operations as a percentage of net revenue was **24.3%** in FY2024, up **460 basis points** from **19.7%** in FY2023. [1] Americas segmented income from operations as a percentage of net revenue was **38.0%** in FY2024, down **50 basis points** from **38.5%** in FY2023. [2]
Lululemon repurchased **5.1 million shares** in fiscal 2024 (ended **February 2, 2025**) at a total cost, including commissions and excise taxes, of **$1.6 billion**. [1][2]
Lululemon’s net income grew **17.1%** from fiscal 2023 to fiscal 2024 (fiscal year ended February 2, 2025), increasing from **$1,550,190 thousand** to **$1,814,616 thousand**. [1]

In Under Armour’s fiscal year ended March 31, 2025, total net revenues decreased **$537.6 million (9.4%)** to **$5.164 billion**. By region: [1]

- **North America:** decreased **$399.5 million (11.4%)**, to **$3.106 billion** from **$3.505 billion** in fiscal 2024. [1]  
- **EMEA:** increased **$4.7 million (0.4%)**, to **$1.087 billion** from **$1.082 billion**. [1]  
- **Asia-Pacific:** decreased **$117.6 million (13.5%)**, to **$755.4 million** from **$873.0 million**. [1]  
- **Latin America:** decreased **$14.1 million (6.1%)**, to **$215.4 million** from **$229.5 million**. [1]

Under Armour’s gross margin increased by approximately 180 basis points to 47.9% in Fiscal 2025 (year ended March 31, 2025). The improvement was primarily driven by:

- **130 basis points** from supply-chain benefits, specifically lower freight and product costs.
- **Approximately 80 basis points** from pricing benefits, largely reflecting less discounting and promotional activity in its direct-to-consumer channel. [1]

These gains were partly offset by **30 basis points** of unfavorable regional and channel mix and **10 basis points** of unfavorable foreign exchange. [1]

Under Armour expects total pre-tax restructuring and related charges of approximately **$140 million to $160 million** under its 2025 restructuring plan, with the high-end estimate totaling **$160.0 million**. This plan is expected to be substantially complete by the end of Fiscal 2026. [1][2]
The provided excerpts do not state how many people Under Armour employed as of March 31, 2025.

Under Armour faced lower demand in its wholesale channel—particularly in North America and Asia-Pacific—and deliberately reduced discounting and promotional activity in its direct-to-consumer channel, especially e-commerce. These factors contributed to total net-revenue decline of 9.4% in fiscal 2025 (year ended March 31, 2025). [1]

Supporting detail:
- Wholesale revenue declined 8.1% and direct-to-consumer revenue declined 10.5% in fiscal 2025. [1]
- North America revenue fell 11.4% and Asia-Pacific revenue fell 13.5% in fiscal 2025. [1]
- Apparel revenue declined primarily from lower unit sales and unfavorable channel mix; footwear revenue declined due to lower unit sales, lower average selling prices, and unfavorable channel mix. [2]
- License revenue declined primarily because of lower revenue from North American licensing partners. [2]

Columbia Sportswear’s consolidated operating margin for 2024 versus 2023 is not directly provided in the excerpts. The excerpts report operating income of **$270.741 million in fiscal 2024** and **$310.284 million in fiscal 2023**, but do not provide consolidated net sales needed to calculate operating margin. [1]

For context, gross margin was **50.2% in fiscal 2024**, versus **49.6% in fiscal 2023**. [2]
Columbia Sportswear’s net sales decreased by **3%** in fiscal year 2024 (ended December 31, 2024), to **$3,368,582 thousand**, from **$3,487,203 thousand** in fiscal year 2023. [1][2]

Columbia Sportswear’s U.S. net sales declined by $173.2 million, or 8%, in fiscal 2024 (year ended December 31, 2024), primarily because of lower U.S. wholesale sales and lower e-commerce sales. [1]

- Wholesale sales declined because Spring and Fall 2024 orders were lower amid retailer cautiousness, including the transition to non-PFAS product chemistry, changes in promotional practices, and a difficult competitive environment. [1]
- DTC e-commerce sales declined due to a challenging e-commerce environment for outdoor brands, greater competition in the outdoor-lifestyle category, and Columbia’s decision to de-emphasize promotions on Columbia.com under its ACCELERATE Growth Strategy. [1]
- These declines were partly offset by growth in brick-and-mortar sales, driven primarily by temporary clearance locations and new stores. [1]

Columbia Sportswear’s business is **highly seasonal**: sales are weighted substantially toward the third and fourth quarters (the fall/winter season), whereas operating costs are distributed more evenly across the year. [1][2][3]

For fiscal year ended December 31, 2024, **over 60% of net sales** and **over 90% of operating income** were realized in the second half of the year. [3] Cash and short-term-investment balances generally reach their low point just before the U.S. holiday season, then rise in the fourth quarter as wholesale receivables are collected and DTC sales occur. [4]

Red Sea disruptions lengthened inbound transit times for Fall 2024 inventory. Columbia expected transit times to remain elevated—and transit pricing to become less favorable—until the conflict is resolved. [1]

More broadly, the company identified the Red Sea conflict as a geopolitical risk that can constrain ocean, air and trucking capacity or disrupt ports and borders, potentially delaying deliveries, hindering fulfillment of wholesale and direct-to-consumer demand, and raising freight and distribution costs. [2]

In Deckers’ fiscal year 2025 (ended March 31, 2025), **HOKA grew faster than UGG**:

- **HOKA:** Net sales increased **23.6% to $2,233,090**. Growth was driven by higher demand for performance products; wholesale growth reflected market-share gains and new distribution points with key partners, while DTC growth was driven by global consumer acquisition and retention. [1][2]
- **UGG:** Net sales increased **13.1% to $2,531,351**. Growth came from higher global demand across wholesale and DTC, particularly internationally; wholesale benefited from year-round product franchises and brand-enhancing retail partners, while DTC benefited from global consumer acquisition and retention. [1][2]

Deckers’ gross margin increased to **57.9% from 55.6%** in fiscal year 2025 (ended March 31, 2025), a **230-basis-point** increase, primarily because of:  

- **Favorable brand and product mix**, with higher-margin products comprising a greater share of growth.  
- **More full-price selling**, primarily for UGG, including **reduced closeouts to the wholesale channel**.  
- These gains were **partially offset by unfavorable changes in freight costs**. [1][2]

Deckers decided to phase out standalone operations for the Koolaburra brand to focus on its most significant organic opportunities. It closed Koolaburra.com on March 31, 2025, and plans to wind down Koolaburra in the wholesale channel by the end of calendar year 2025. [1][2]

Deckers employed approximately **5,500 employees** as of March 31, 2025, the end of its fiscal year 2025. This figure includes approximately 2,000 retail-store employees and excludes temporary and seasonal employees. [1]
HOKA represented approximately **44.8%** of Deckers’ total fiscal 2025 net sales: **$2,233,090** of **$4,985,612** (fiscal year ended March 31, 2025). [1]
